fixer.title: chat: fix flaky Draw atlas tests leaking into later suites

introducer.title: perf: reduce chat rendering overhead with compositor-driven Draw

cases.mechanism: The live-atlas remount test released the production shared cache at zero references and then reacquired the same atlas key, forcing serial SVG decode, canvas rasterization, and blob encoding repeatedly in one test.
cases.symptom: Repeated full-atlas generation made the browser test slow enough to exceed its 15-second timeout on throttled or slow CI agents.
cases.fixedBehavior: The added test-local cache survives zero-reference intervals for the test lifetime, so hide/remount cycles reuse the first decoded atlas rather than repeating the 320-frame rasterization for each reacquire.
cases.evidence: The base test constructed ChatWorkingLogo without an acquireAtlas override, so each remount used acquireChatWorkingLogoAtlas. That shared wrapper disposes its per-window cache when the last reference is released (chatWorkingLogoAtlas.ts:119-151), while hiding/removing the logo clears its atlas request; the same test then hides and remounts the logo repeatedly. Each resulting cold acquire calls createChatWorkingLogoAtlas, whose serial loop decodes and rasterizes 320 frames (chatWorkingLogoAtlas.ts:203-275). The changed test instead owns one ChatWorkingLogoAtlasCache and routes every reacquire through it, whose released completed entries remain reusable until cache teardown.
